arxiv-2012-07563.title: A Practical Approach towards Causality Mining in Clinical Text using Active Transfer Learning Journal: Journal of Biomedical Informatics
arxiv-2012-07563.creator: Musarrat Hussain, Fahad Ahmed Satti, Jamil Hussain, Taqdir Ali, Syed Imran Ali, Hafiz Syed Muhammad Bilal, Gwang Hoon Park, Sungyoung Lee
arxiv-2012-07563.description: Abstract Objective: Causality mining is an active research area, which requires the application of state-of-the-art natural language processing techniques. In the healthcare domain, medical experts create clinical text to overcome the limitation of well-defined and schema driven information systems. The objective of this research work is to create a framework, which can convert clinical text into causal knowledge.

arxiv-2106-16156.creator: Jun-Ming Zhu
arxiv-2106-16156.description: Abstract . Jacobi’s triple product identity is proved from one of Euler’s q q -exponential functions in an elementary way. 1. Introduction We suppose |q|<1 and, as usual, the q -Pochhammer symbols are defined respectively by (a;q)_{\infty}=\prod_{n=0}^{\infty}(1-aq^{n})\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad(a;q)_{n}=\frac{(a;q)_{\infty}}{(aq^{n};q)_{\infty}} for any integer n . Jacobi’s triple product identity is one of the most important series-product identities.

arxiv-2203-14008.title: Parameter Space of Morse Oscillator
arxiv-2203-14008.creator: M.Y. Tan, M.S. Nurisya, H. Zainuddin
arxiv-2203-14008.description: Abstract We present the analysis of mathematical structure of SU(2) group, specifically the commutation relation between raising and lowering operators of the Morse oscillator. The relationship between the commutator of operators and other parameters of Morse oscillator is investigated. We show that the mathematical structure of operators which depends on the parameters of Morse oscillator may change our conventional expectation.

arxiv-2403-13173.title: GerontoVis: Data Visualization at the Confluence of Aging Volume: 43 Issue: 3
arxiv-2403-13173.creator: Zack While 1 , R. Jordan Crouser 2 , and Ali Sarvghad 1 1 Manning College of Information and Computer Sciences, University of Massachusetts, Amherst, USA 2 Department of Computer Science, Smith College, Northampton, USA
arxiv-2403-13173.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zack While 1 , R. Jordan Crouser 2 , and Ali Sarvghad 1 1 Manning College of Information and Computer Sciences, University of Massachusetts, Amherst, USA 2 Department of Computer Science, Smith College, Northampton, USA. Despite the explosive growth of the aging population worldwide, older adults have been largely overlooked by visualization research. This paper is a critical reflection on the underrepresentation of older adults in visualization research.

arxiv-2501-05731.title: Diving Deep: Forecasting Sea Surface Temperatures and Anomalies
arxiv-2501-05731.creator: Ding Ning, Varvara Vetrova (✉), Karin R. Bryan, Yun Sing Koh, Andreas Voskou, N’Dah Jean Kouagou, Arnab Sharma
arxiv-2501-05731.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ding Ning, Varvara Vetrova (✉), Karin R. Bryan, Yun Sing Koh, Andreas Voskou, N’Dah Jean Kouagou, Arnab Sharma. This overview paper details the findings from the Diving Deep: Forecasting Sea Surface Temperatures and Anomalies Challenge at the European Conference on Machine Learning and Principles and Practice of Knowledge Discovery in Databases (ECML PKDD) 2024. The challenge focused on the data-driven predictability of global sea surface temperatures (SSTs), a key factor in climate forecasting, ecosystem management, fisheries management, and climate change monitoring.

britannica-1911-ewing-thomas.description: Article 'Ewing, Thomas' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born near the present West Liberty, West Virginia, on the 28th of December 1789. His father, George Ewing, settled at Lancaster, Fairfield county, Ohio, in 1792. Thomas graduated at Ohio University, Athens, Ohio, in 1815, and in August 1816 was admitted to the bar at Lancaster, where he won high rank as an advocate.

pmc-11325593.title: The Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score correlates with epidural spinal cord compression -a retrospective cohort of 256 surgically treated patients with spinal metastases
pmc-11325593.creator: Lukas Bobinski, Joel Axelsson, Jonathan Melhus, Josefin Åkerstedt, Johan Wänman
pmc-11325593.description: BackgroundBone metastases can compromise the integrity of the spinal canal and cause epidural spinal cord compression (ESCC). The Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score (SINS) was developed in order to evaluate spinal instability due to a neoplastic process. The SINS has reached wide acceptance among clinicans but its prognostic value is still controversial.

pmc-11525191.title: Party preferences for climate policy and the renewable energy transition in Spain’s multilevel democracy
pmc-11525191.creator: Joan Enguer
pmc-11525191.description: The growing influence of regional governments in shaping climate policy and driving the renewable energy transition in multilevel democracies like Spain provides incentives for parties in favor of decentralization to emphasize these issues. Recent research has shown that such parties act as climate pioneers at the regional tier of government, driven by their desire to assert stronger subnational authority.

pmc-11588415.title: The clinical usefulness of guideline-based strategies with and without the role of nonspecific symptoms to predict urinary tract infections in nursing homes: a decision curve analysis
pmc-11588415.creator: Sacha Kuil, Menno de Jong, Caroline Schneeberger, Frank van Leth
pmc-11588415.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objective:The aim of this study was to assess the clinical value of urinary tract infections (UTIs) guideline algorithms and the role of nonspecific symptoms to support clinical decision-making in nursing home residents.Design:In a preplanned secondary analysis of a cross-sectional study including nursing home residents with a presumed UTI, 2 prediction models were used in a decision curve analysis (DCA): (1) guideline-based and (2) extended: nonspecific symptom(s) added to the guideline model.

pmc-12406480.title: Separable cryo-microneedle patches delivery with capsaicin integrated mesoporous dopamine for obesity treatment
pmc-12406480.creator: Jingjing Gan, Lingyu Sun, Wenjuan Tang, Yuanjin Zhao, Yan Bi
pmc-12406480.description: Microneedle patch encapsulated with active medication holds significant potential promise in the realm of anti-obesity therapy. Nevertheless, the improvement of actives delivery efficiency remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we present novel separable cryo-microneedles patches delivered with capsaicin integrated mesoporous dopamine (mPDA) for obesity treatment through activating TRPV1 and inducing lipid droplet dissolution.

pmc-13059452.title: Barriers to optimal central venous catheter training: a qualitative study of physician experiences
pmc-13059452.creator: Joy Abou Farah, Kipum Lee, Jin E Kim-Mozeleski, Alexia El Khoury, Zainab Albar, Christopher Ladikos, Demetra Yianas, Noah Carty, Tina M Lewis, Kendra Marianne Gardiner, Elie Saade
pmc-13059452.description: BackgroundCentral venous catheter (CVC) placement is a high-risk procedure requiring advanced training to minimize complications. Despite widespread use of various training approaches, little is known about how physicians experience CVC training in practice. The authors carried out this study to explore the experiences of physicians with central venous catheter (CVC) training and to identify opportunities for improvement.

pmc-13097555.title: The Immediate Effects of Vibrotexture Shoe Insoles on Quiet Standing Balance and Lower Limb Muscle Activity in Healthy Young Adults
pmc-13097555.creator: Megan Trotman, Avni Hurkat, Kylie Tucker, Thomas Cattagni, Anna L Hatton
pmc-13097555.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionShoe insoles that provide a single source of plantar sensory stimulus, such as texture or vibration, can improve measures of standing balance. Vibrotexture insoles, designed to provide multiple sources of sensory stimuli, may provide greater benefits.

pmc-13105586.title: Quality of life and functional outcomes after rectal sparing approaches following neoadjuvant therapy for rectal cancer: a prospective cohort multicentre study
pmc-13105586.creator: Teresa Gavaruzzi, Paola Del Bianco, Laura Gavagna, Quoc Riccardo Bao, Daniela Rega, Angelo Restivo, Simona Deidda, Claudio Belluco, Andrea Lauretta, Carlo Aschele, Antonino Spinelli, Carmela Cervone, Lucia Perna, Francesco Bianco, Giacomo Sarzo, Claudio Coco, Giuditta Chiloiro, Andrea Muratore, Alfr
pmc-13105586.description: Background:This prospective observational multicenter cohort study aimed to establish the functional outcomes and quality of life (QoL) of patients with rectal cancer who showed a major (mCR) or complete clinical response (cCR) after neoadjuvant therapy and underwent a rectum-sparing approach (watch and wait, WW, or local excision, LE).

pmc-13237058.title: Enhanced water desalination via PVDF-chabazite mixed matrix membranes in vacuum membrane distillation
pmc-13237058.creator: Maksymilian Plata-Gryl, Francesco Galiano, Francesca Russo, Rokaya Ben Abed, Alberto Figoli, Roger Gläser, Roberto Castro-Muñoz
pmc-13237058.description: Vacuum membrane distillation is foreseen as a membrane unit operation capable of providing access to drinking water in the future, through the saline water desalination. To increase the permeation of standard hydrophobic membranes, such as PVDF, mixed matrix membranes are defined as the next generation of membranes and prepared by adding a filler into the polymer phase.

pmc-13374470.title: Prevalence of zero-dose vaccination and its associated factors in urban areas of Somali region, Ethiopia: a mixed-methods approach
pmc-13374470.creator: Abdifatah Elmi, Mahamed Ibrahim, Abdi Farah, Ahmed Tahir, Abdisalan Muktar, Abdirazak Mohamoud Abdilahi
pmc-13374470.description: IntroductionDespite global progress in immunisation, vaccine coverage remains uneven in many low- and middle-income countries. Urbanisation has widened disparities, particularly among children in informal settlements. Ethiopia has a high zero-dose burden, with the Somali region identified as a hotspot. However, urban areas in this region remain understudied.
